scenes.headline: How an open training run changes course halfway
scenes.sub: A huge mixture of experts, its changelog, and the forecast that referees it.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cinder! Marin is training a giant mixture of experts in public, and changed it several times on the way. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Every mid-run change is judged against a forecast fitted on small copies of the same recipe before the big run started.
scenes.mark: a forecast fitted on small copies
scenes.say: Before launch, they trained the same recipe at four small widths and fitted a forecast. Every surprise since is checked against that line.

scenes.title: A sphere for every matrix
scenes.text: W' = |W| x unit(W - lr x |W| x U)
scenes.say: Their optimizer keeps every weight matrix at a fixed size.

parts.note: step along the update, sized to the weight
parts.say: It steps along an orthogonalized update, scaled to the weight.

parts.note: then rescale back to the original size
parts.say: Then it rescales the result back onto its sphere. The size never changes.

steps.say: Each layer's attention heads read the token, and every head passes through its own gate.
The gate scales a head between zero and two. It starts at one.

steps.note: the free parameter is where scale went
steps.say: Almost every matrix here has its size pinned. The gate's weights are not, and they grew until early layers nearly shut attention off.
Loss was on track, so the fix was gentle: a small weight decay on the gate, fading to zero by the last step.

left.title: Pooled-wave transport
left.say: The run launched with fixed-size buffers. Anything past capacity was dropped, about three percent of expert assignments.

right.title: Ragged all-to-all
right.say: Mid-run they swapped in a ragged exchange that sends exactly what each expert receives. Drops fell to nearly zero.

scenes.title: Hardware utilisation, same run
scenes.note: model FLOPs utilisation, per the team's W&B report
scenes.say: New attention kernels and an expert layer that skips padding took utilisation from twenty one to twenty seven percent.

steps.say: Solid lines are the real run. The dashed line is the forecast, adjusted for the new data.
Since about a third of the way in, the run has sat right on it.

scenes.text: A forecast fitted before launch turns every weird norm plot into one question: is held-out loss still on the line?
scenes.mark: is held-out loss still on the line?
scenes.say: A forecast fitted before launch turns every strange plot into one question. Is held-out loss still on the line?

recap: Small copies forecast the big run
scenes.say: Forecast first. Then change only what the forecast can referee.
